title: Observability for audit-export: dashboards + alerts (latency, success rate, DLQ, connector errors)
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Goal
Create a complete, SIEM/enterprise-ready observability surface for audit-export (beta) that allows SRE + oncall to detect and diagnose: delivery failures, delivery lag, connector-specific error spikes, DLQ growth/poison pills, and backlog runaway. Must work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (with Private-friendly defaults).

Scope
- Dashboards (Grafana) + alert rules (Prometheus/Alertmanager) for:
  1) Export delivery success rate (end-to-end and per connector)
  2) Delivery latency (p50/p95/p99 end-to-end)
  3) Backlog depth / backlog age (if available) per destination
  4) DLQ volume + DLQ write rate + oldest DLQ item age
  5) Connector error spikes (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3) with error-class breakdown (auth, throttling, 5xx, schema/validation, payload too large)
  6) Worker health (restarts/crashloop, queue consumer lag, retry storm indicators)
- Runbook hooks: all pages must link to the existing backlog drain/replay runbook and include "top 3" likely causes + first checks.
- Metrics naming + labels standardization and cardinality guardrails.

Non-goals
- Building a full customer-facing Console analytics dashboard (Console will consume a small subset via health endpoints; see ENG-13928/ENG-13930).
- Long-term metrics retention policy changes (handled by platform observability).

Reference / context
- SLOs are defined in Confluence: eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/audit-export-slos
- Runbook: eng-sre/runbooks/audit-export-backlog-drain-replay
- Connector semantics & error taxonomy: ADR-0218 (Splunk), design spec on filtering/delivery guarantees.

Proposed metrics (minimum required)
Note: exact metric names can be adjusted, but we need consistent labels: deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), destination_type (splunk|datadog|s3), destination_id (caution), tenant_id (DO NOT include), workspace_id (DO NOT include). Prefer destination_id only on logs/traces; avoid in high-cardinality metrics.

Counters
- audit_export_events_attempted_total{destination_type}
- audit_export_events_delivered_total{destination_type}
- audit_export_events_failed_total{destination_type, error_class}
- audit_export_batches_delivered_total{destination_type}
- audit_export_dlq_written_total{destination_type, reason}

Histograms
- audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds{destination_type}  (end-to-end from enqueue -> sink ack/commit)
- audit_export_connector_request_latency_seconds{destination_type}

Gauges
- audit_export_backlog_depth{destination_type}
- audit_export_backlog_oldest_age_seconds{destination_type} (if available; else derive from checkpoints)
- audit_export_dlq_depth{destination_type}
- audit_export_last_success_timestamp_seconds{destination_type} (exporter-reported; use carefully)

Derived / recording rules
- Delivery success rate per destination_type: delivered / attempted over 5m + 30m windows
- Error budget burn style panels (fast burn vs slow burn) for delivery failures

Dashboards (deliverables)
1) "Audit Export – Overview" (for oncall)
- Success rate (5m/30m), end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99), backlog depth + oldest age, DLQ depth, top connector errors (by class)
- Segmented by deployment_mode + destination_type
- Single panel: "Destinations with no successful delivery in >N minutes" (uses last_success)

2) "Audit Export – Connector Deep Dive" (for debugging)
- Per connector request latency, response codes (where applicable), retries/backoff, throttling signals (429s), auth failures (401/403), payload size violations
- Splunk-specific: HEC ACK enabled vs disabled (if label exists), HEC 5xx spike indicator
- Datadog-specific: intake endpoint region breakdown, 429 rate
- S3-specific: put-object errors, KMS errors, access denied

3) "Audit Export – Worker / Queue" (for reliability)
- Consumer lag (if exposed), retry queue depth, worker restarts, CPU/mem (Private), circuit breaker / backpressure indicator (ENG-13932 may add signals)

Alerts (deliverables)
Alerts should be actionable and avoid paging on expected transient issues. Paging vs ticket thresholds should align with audit-export SLOs.

Paging alerts (P1 page)
- Delivery failure rate fast burn: success_rate < 99.0% for 10m (per destination_type, per deployment_mode) AND attempted_total above minimum traffic threshold
- Delivery latency: p95 end-to-end latency > 300s for 15m (Hosted/Dedicated). For Private, default to warning unless customer opts into paging.
- Backlog runaway: backlog_oldest_age_seconds > 900s for 15m OR backlog_depth growing monotonically for 30m (if we can implement a robust rule)
- DLQ growth: dlq_written_total rate > X/min for 10m OR dlq_depth > 1000 AND increasing

Ticket alerts (non-paging)
- Connector auth failures sustained (401/403) for 15m (often requires customer action; should generate a support playbook entry)
- Throttling sustained (429) for 30m (should suggest batching/backoff tuning)
- Schema/validation failures ("schema") > 0 for 10m (indicates bug/regression; should page only if widespread)

Alert routing
- Route to #oncall-sre + pager policy for Hosted/Dedicated.
- For Private: alerts should be present but default routed to #private-support / ticket unless explicitly enabled per customer environment.

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboards are merged into observability-pack and deployed to staging + prod.
- Oncall can identify, within 5 minutes, whether an incident is due to: (a) destination auth, (b) throttling, (c) connector 5xx, (d) queue backlog/retry storm, (e) poison pill / DLQ.
- Alerts include runbook links + initial triage steps.
- Metric label set reviewed for cardinality (no tenant/workspace IDs).
- Basic alert tuning completed using staging load test + one beta tenant shadow traffic (where available).

Testing plan
- Use audit-export-test-matrix scenarios:
  - Splunk: force 401, force 5xx, enable HEC ACK and simulate missing ACK, throttle
  - Datadog: 429s + regional endpoint misconfig
  - S3: access denied + KMS deny
  - Inject poison pill event -> DLQ
  - Induce worker crashloop -> restart panels/alerts

Implementation notes
- Prefer recording rules for success rate + latency SLO style panels to reduce query cost.
- Where possible, keep destination_id out of metrics; use exemplars/traces/logs for per-destination drilldown.
- Ensure that exporter logs include a stable error_id / request_id for correlation with Console + support tickets.

comments: 2025-02-03 (Allison Grant): Marking as P0 for beta readiness. We need a single overview dashboard for oncall plus connector deep dive. Also please make sure we can distinguish customer misconfig (401/403) vs our infra (5xx/backlog).

2025-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): +1. For paging thresholds: let’s align to audit-export SLO doc. Also we need a clear backlog oldest-age signal. If we can’t compute it reliably, at least alert on "no successful delivery" + backlog growth.
2025-02-09 (Aisha Bello): Drafted dashboard panels in staging. Main gap: backlog_oldest_age not yet emitted; using checkpoint age as proxy. Waiting on ENG-13923/ENG-13928 to finalize metric surfaces.

2025-02-12 (Rafael Mendes): Please add direct links from alert annotations to runbook section anchors ("Splunk 5xx" / "Auth failures" / "DLQ poison pill"). Also need a non-paging alert for sustained 401/403 so Support can proactively reach out.

2025-02-16 (Aisha Bello): Implemented recording rules for success_rate_5m and latency_p95_5m by destination_type + deployment_mode. Removed destination_id label from counters after cardinality review. Added log-based drilldown for destination_id (example query in dashboard).

2025-02-19 (Allison Grant): Reviewed PR 0331. Looks good. Request: add a "retry storm" panel (retry attempts per delivered event) and a panel showing top error_class over 30m to catch slow-burn schema issues.

2025-02-20 (Aisha Bello): Added retry storm ratio + top error_class. PR updated and re-requested review. If we hit false positives on DLQ alert in prod, we’ll tune the rate threshold after first beta onboarding.
